links_touching_record.rationale: Implementation element FB2-SW-IMP-000002 is the code location in which the reference project's FB2-SW-DSN-000002 limit-comparison and diagnosis-raising responsibilities are carried, and it declares the per-cell debounce counter that design requires and the pinned source does not contain as an explicit not_in_source proposal. The link runs from the implementation to the design per master prompt section 13.

The SOA detailed design carries the constraint 'Debounce count configurable (default: 2)'. This change moves the default to 3, and makes the design's existing reset_debounce action load-bearing, so the design is a declared target.

The SOA design already specifies the DEBOUNCING -> IDLE transition with the action reset_debounce, so the design is correct and is not revised. It is a declared target of the change because the divergence was located here and the absence of a revision is a decision that belongs on the record.
FB2-SW-SWR-000002 is allocated to the reference project's FB2-SW-DSN-000002 as the software requirement whose implementation that design details. Direction is requirement -> design element.

FB2-SW-DSN-000005 refines FB2-SW-DSN-000002: the source side is the lower-level detailed specification and the target side is the parent architecture record. DSN-000002 allocates the SOA element and states its diagnosis interfaces at architecture level; DSN-000005 specifies the internals - the split between the evaluator in soa.c and the limit providers in soa_cfg.c, the three-tier MOL/RSL/MSL nesting, the validity-bit gating, and the fact that SOA_CheckSlaveTemperatures has an empty body. One correction of fact belongs on this link rather than on the records: DSN-000002 already carries design_level=detailed_design while its own standards_mappings name SWE.2 with the rationale "Software architectural design", so its level token and its process reference disagree. DSN-000005 is the record that carries the ISO 26262-6 clause 8.4 content and the SWE.3 reference; the disagreement on DSN-000002 is recorded here because that record is not edited by this change, as editing it would invalidate nine review digests that record its current content.

The SOA design record's interfaces field is a signal table naming fault_request as bool and violation_details as a struct at event rate. FB2-SW-IFS-000002 replaces it with the four declared elements of the module, three of which return void and register diagnosis events, and the fourth of which is declared and called on the 10 ms cycle and does nothing. It refines FB2-SW-DSN-000002 and sits alongside FB2-SW-DSN-000005, which designs the debounce internally and still carries no interface contract.

The redundancy-management interface refines the SOA voltage-monitoring design record, because the validity flags this interface produces are an input to the SOA checks that record describes. The design record states that the SOA module judges measured values against configured limits; it does not say where the judgement of whether those values may be trusted comes from. This link declares that dependency rather than leaving it implicit, and the direction is specification refines design because the interface is the finer statement about the input boundary.

integrity.anchor_registry_note: The corpus provenance gate verifies each anchor against the file that anchor names and stores no registry-level digest of its own. This digest is recorded so a signature also pins which anchor set was in force.
integrity.verbatim_block_note: The block in section 3 is the file's decoded text with any single trailing newline removed, which is what the markdown fences require. `record_sha256` above is over the raw file bytes and is the digest a signature refers to; this one is over the text as embedded, so a verifier can compare either.

shape_note: Deliberately not shaped like a corpus record: no top-level id, profile, artifact_type or source_refs, so that generating packets cannot change any coverage number. See the module docstring of make_review_packets.py.

_contract.digest_note: The digests below are already filled in. Copy them; do not type them. Run `make_review_packets.py --transcribe FB2-SW-DSN-000002` to have them printed as a pasteable block.
_contract.grant_is: any value other than "pending" or absent
required_elements: 2. approved_by - a named individual, not a role and not a team

3. role - a role_id declared in role-and-review-policy.json#/roles - plus independence{owner_role, satisfied, evidence, policy_ref}; the approving role must differ from owner_role AND from the author of the last content revision
4. date - ISO-8601, checked by grammar and by parse

5. review_packet{path, sha256, record_sha256_at_signing}; path must resolve to a packet.json on disk under docs/artifacts/reviews/packets/ or docs/artifacts/reviews/signed/; sha256 must equal that file's bytes now; record_sha256_at_signing must equal this packet's integrity.record_sha256; target.record_id and target.profile must both name this record
6. a revision_history entry whose author is the approving role and whose description records the approval and cites the signed packet

signature_block._packet_sha256_note: The digest of this packet.json's own bytes. It is deliberately left null rather than filled, because a file cannot contain its own digest. Compute it with `shasum -a 256`, or use `--transcribe`, which resolves it.
signature_block._recording: Transcribe a completed signature into the record as human_approval_status plus an approval_evidence.human_approval block plus a revision_history entry naming the reviewer and citing this packet, and archive the signed packet under docs/artifacts/reviews/signed/.
signature_block._rule: Empty by construction. No automated process may fill this. Filling it in is the only thing that changes human_approval_status on the record. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus rule human_approval_rejected is an EVIDENCE requirement, not a prohibition: a properly evidenced approval is ACCEPTED and keeps `corpus.py check` green, while a bare grant value is still rejected. What the validator reads is contract.approval_evidence_block below; it fails if any of its six elements is missing, and the finding names which.

signature_policy: The signature block below is empty by construction. This tool has no code path that writes a decision, an approval, a signature or an execution verdict. Filling it is a human action. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus ACCEPTS a properly evidenced approval rather than banning the value outright, so this rule now has to carry the evidence contract in full: see signature_block._contract.
